title: Clean canonical repository entry points after the clean-break decision
purpose: Remove stale current-state claims from canonical repository entry points after adoption of the clean-break trajectory. Preserve historical architecture evidence while making README, contribution, governance, architecture, roadmap and legacy Player documentation agree with RC718 as the frozen legacy product and ARC-WP-022 as the next mandatory gate.
invariants: RC718 source, artifact, runtime, tests and learner data remain unchanged.
ARC-WP-021 clean-break trajectory remains the canonical product direction.
The learnit-identity-v1 taxonomy remains accepted while the continuity strategy remains superseded.
ARC-WP-022 remains the next mandatory gate and no new-generation implementation is authorized.
Historical reference-v1 documents remain available but are explicitly non-canonical for current status.
No generated archive, credential, build output or Player working file is added.
Backend, accounts, synchronization, catalog, commerce, tenancy and marketplace remain held.
requiredEvidence: Exact stale statements and their canonical replacements are recorded in the repository cleanliness audit.
The repository validator continues to reject generated archives and credential-like files.
The gitignore excludes build outputs, local data, credentials and archives.
No pull request is open at the audit baseline.
Repository governance and PR-scope checks pass on the exact cleanup head.
adversarialTests: Fail if a canonical entry point still claims RC715 is current or promoted.
Fail if an entry point claims Player source remains outside the repository.
Fail if ARC-WP-000 or QA-WP-010 is described as the next gate.
Fail if the pre-clean-break migration roadmap is presented as current.
Fail if historical reference-v1 material is deleted or silently rewritten as implemented reality.
Fail if any Player source, test, build, contract, artifact or workflow file changes.
Fail if ARC-WP-022 is represented as implementation already accepted.
nonGoals: Deleting historical work packages, reviews or evidence.
Changing the identity taxonomy or clean-break decision.
Cleaning remote branches that cannot be proven stale from repository evidence.
independentReview: Repository governance validates the work-package and governor-state schemas.
PR scope validates the exact documentation and governance paths.
The governor checks every current-status claim against main and accepted decisions.
Contradictory review confirms that historical evidence is preserved and implementation remains held.
rollback: Revert the cleanup merge. No source, artifact, learner data, build, contract or external system is affected.
